title: upgrade attention kernels: FlashAttentionV2 + fused-rope/rotary op optimizations
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: reduce tail-latency and per-token compute for attention-heavy workloads by upstreaming FlashAttentionV2 kernels where available and adding fused rotary/rope and qkv-fusion fast paths. This PR integrates a vetted FlashAttentionV2 implementation into the serving runtime, exposes a runtime kernel selector, and implements fused operators for rotary/rope application and qkv projection that reduce memory traffic and kernel launches. Implementation summary: 1) Add flashattentionv2 backend module with CUDA/ROCm dispatch and fallbacks to our existing optimized kernels. 2) Implement fused_rope operator that applies rotary embeddings in-place using vectorized loads when sequence length is large and dtype is float16/bfloat16. 3) Add qkv_fused GEMM path that emits a single matmul for combined QKV for common transformer blocks and uses persistent shared-memory tiling for small-to-medium batch sizes. 4) Kernel selector heuristics: at model load we sample a few latency microbenchmarks to choose between flashattentionv2, native_fused, or scalar_fallback paths based on sequence length, batch size, dtype, and hardware architecture. 5) Continuous batching integration: ensure KV cache compatibility with fused qkv and FlashAttentionV2 by adding KV reshape/stride adapters and unit tests to avoid extra copies. Benchmarks: internal benchmarks on A100 and H100 show median per-token throughput improvement of 18-34% for GPT-like decoder models with seq_len 128-2048 and 8-20 token batches; P95 latency improved 12-28% in production-like traces. Memory peak reduced by ~10% for bfloat16 workloads due to in-place rope and fused qkv. Testing and safety: unit kernels validated against reference attention implementation across fp16/bf16/fp32; added regression tests for KV cache correctness across rolling generation and beam search. Added end-to-end smoke tests in perf-canary harness. Backwards compatibility: fallbacks ensure models run on older drivers or where FlashAttentionV2 is incompatible; runtime selector can be forced via REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREF envvar for customer troubleshooting. Rollout plan: gated rollout to 25% of hosted traffic for 48 hours with extended telemetry; dedicated clusters opt-in via config. Related work: follows prototype in ENG-4982 and addresses regressions found in SUP-724 incident. Notes: this PR intentionally keeps API surface unchanged; any user-facing flags are behind feature gates.
commits: feat: add flashattentionv2 backend and kernel selector; feat: fused_rope operator with in-place path; perf: qkv_fused GEMM path and tiling; test: add kernel unit tests and kv-cache regression tests; ci: add microbench harness for kernel selection sampling
review_comments: Evan Cho: Please add a fallback when driver older than 525 is detected; observed illegal instruction on our H100 testbed. Author: added a driver check and fallthrough to native_fused, added test in ci matrix.

Luis Moretti: Can we avoid sampling at model load for very latency-sensitive paths? Suggested a cached heuristics table per model signature. Author: added heuristics cache keyed by (model_hash, device_arch) and TTL 7 days.
Priya Nair: Add more coverage for beam search with kv-cache edge cases where sequence lengths vary. Author: added regression cases and fixed a stride bug in kv adapter.
Infra CI: initial GPU matrix job failed on ROCm; reproduction pointed to missing rocblas symbol. Author: split ROCm build step and updated third_party build flags; reran and passed.
ci_details: Matrix: linux-gpu(A100/H100)-cuda build and tests, linux-gpu-roc build, unit tests, lint, perf microbench. Initial run: ROCm job failed on symbol export, fix applied and rerun. Final: all checks passed. Perf microbench flagged a ~3% deviation on one test which was explained by background noise; re-run confirmed improvement.
release_notes: Performance: Faster attention kernels via FlashAttentionV2 and fused rotary/qkv ops. Reduced per-token latency and memory for many decoder workloads. Rollout behind feature gate. See docs/notes/flashattentionv2-migration.md for known compatibility notes.
notes_for_ops: Operators: kernel selector can be overridden with REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREF (values: flashv2,native_fused,scalar). When on-prem customers report issues, ask for device_report and set REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREF=native_fused. For Dedicated clusters, use feature flag kernels.flashv2.enabled=false to opt-out.
